title: Equipment support requirement example
summary: Users identify equipment, submit a problem, review feedback and confirm the resulting status.
content: A responsive equipment support page lets a user find an asset, enter a problem description, submit a request and review its status. Required information is checked before submission. Keep recovery guidance visible after a failed attempt. Requirement product user story feature scope page constraint.

title: Text-only equipment support layout
summary: A heading, equipment selector, problem input, submit control and local feedback region form a simple support layout.
content: Use a clear page heading and a compact input form. Group the equipment selector and problem description together, followed by a submit button and visible status feedback. Preserve keyboard focus order and use readable labels. This is a project-authored text description, not a screenshot or a copied UI asset. UI reference visual layout control structure screen layout component.

title: Equipment support interaction example
summary: Identify equipment, enter a problem, submit, inspect feedback and confirm or recover.
content: The user selects equipment and enters a problem description. Submitting without required information leaves the form available and shows feedback. A valid submission exposes the resulting request status. A failed operation retains enough information for retry. Interaction flow page state operation step gesture submit confirm retry.

title: Offline support prototype implementation example
summary: Build a self-contained responsive prototype with local state and feedback; do not simulate a real server integration.
content: Implement semantic sections, labelled controls and a feedback region in HTML and CSS. Client-side event handlers update explicit page states. Keep the prototype self-contained and describe it as an offline demonstration, not a deployed ticket system. Frontend implementation responsive webpage HTML prototype layout input field submit.

title: Support prototype validation example
summary: Check missing input, valid submission, visible feedback, keyboard access and recovery guidance.
content: Attempt submission with an empty problem description and inspect the visible feedback. Provide the required input and check the resulting page state. Verify that keyboard users can reach the controls. Inspect the failure path and ensure that recovery guidance is visible. These are authored example checks, not measured pass results.
